name: vscode-veridelta
description: Validate a Veridelta configuration into the Problems panel, run a comparison and open its report, and register veridelta mcp with agent mode.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Veridelta runs the program veridelta.command names, and a workspace's settings can set it.

virtualWorkspaces.description: Veridelta reads configurations and data from files on disk.

veridelta.command.markdownDescription: The words that run Veridelta. A project that runs it through uv sets `["uv", "run", "veridelta"]`. The command runs in the configuration file's folder.

veridelta.run.htmlMaxRows.markdownDescription: Rows per table in the HTML report, passed as `--html-max-rows`. Unset, Veridelta's default of 1000 applies.

veridelta.mcp.allowRowValues.markdownDescription: Let the agent's tools return values from the data, as `veridelta mcp --allow-row-values` does. Off, an agent sees counts, columns, and keys only. Only user settings apply, so a workspace cannot turn it on.

veridelta.mcp.allowQueries.markdownDescription: Let a tool run a side's query as written, as `veridelta mcp --allow-queries` does. Only user settings apply, so a workspace cannot turn it on.

items.patternErrorMessage: A host in lowercase, with no scheme or port, such as db.internal or 10.0.0.5.

veridelta.mcp.allowHosts.markdownDescription: Hosts the agent's tools may connect to, such as a database server, a bucket, or a URL's host, each passed as `veridelta mcp --allow-host`. Write each in lowercase, with no scheme or port. Empty, a tool reads only data on this machine, MotherDuck, Hugging Face, or BigQuery with the server's own credentials. Only user settings apply, so a workspace cannot widen what the agent reaches. Veridelta 0.42.2 has no `--allow-host`, and the setting applies from the release after it.

veridelta.mcp.maxRows.markdownDescription: The most rows, or value map entries, one tool call returns, as `veridelta mcp --max-rows` sets it, up to 1000. Only user settings apply.

scripts.check: npm run lint && npm run format:check && npm run typecheck
scripts.pretest: npm run build && npm run build:tests
scripts.test: npm run test:unit && npm run test:integration
